entries.title: Greetings from sweltering Switzerland
entries.snippet: On the waterfront in Lucerne, Switzerland, soccer fans watched jumbo TVs showing a World Cup match played an ocean away. But the air felt more like the tropics.

entries.title: IAEA chief says inspectors will visit nuclear sites under Iran-U.S. interim deal
entries.snippet: The head of the U.N.'s nuclear agency has signaled that Iranian nuclear enrichment sites would be visited by his inspectors, a day after the U.S. and Iran offered contradictory remarks about the issue.

entries.title: Congress passes major housing bill. And, Mamdani-backed candidates sweep NYC primaries
entries.snippet: Congress has passed the largest housing affordability bill in decades. And all three candidates endorsed by New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani have won their primaries.

entries.title: 4 ways to design a dreamy summer, according to a happiness expert
entries.snippet: Don't let the season fly by. Gretchen Rubin, host of the Happier podcast, shares exercises to help you get what you want out of summer. Fill out the printable worksheet and stick it on your fridge.

entries.title: 5 years after the Surfside condo collapse, the toll of the tragedy remains
entries.snippet: Surfside, Florida, is marking five years since a beachfront condominium collapsed, killing 98 people. It was one of the largest structural failures in U.S. history.

entries.title: New York primary could forecast future for Democrats. Here's what you need to know
entries.snippet: New York's primary election highlighted a question the Democratic Party is facing: just how progressive does it want to be? In safe seats, progressives win but in competitive seats, moderates prevail.

entries.title: Why are crisis pregnancy centers saying they can 'rule out' ectopic pregnancy?
entries.snippet: Under President Trump, more federal attention and support has gone towards anti-abortion Christian centers. A watchdog group says many of them mislead patients with promises to "rule out" ectopic pregnancies.

entries.title: Inside the gold-mining town where the Ebola outbreak likely started
entries.snippet: NPR reports from Mongbwalu in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The fight to contain the virus faces obstacles from lack of supplies to residents who doubt that the virus is real.

entries.title: Appeals court allows Trump administration expanded use of speedy deportations
entries.snippet: A federal appeals court on Tuesday allowed the Trump administration to resume carrying out speedy deportations of undocumented migrants throughout the United States, not just near the border.

entries.title: Federal officials plan to offload some warehouses purchased for immigrant detention
entries.snippet: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement is retreating from a plan to use warehouses to hold up to 10,000 people on a single site, dropping a key piece of former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem's $38-billion plan to rapidly expand detention capacity this year.

entries.title: House gives final approval to landmark housing bill aimed at lowering costs
entries.snippet: The legislation represents one of the most sweeping efforts in decades to increase the supply of housing and bring down prices.

entries.snippet: Top allies of New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani have defeated establishment-backed Democrats in New York's congressional primary elections.

entries.title: Maryland Democrats pick their U.S. House nominees as Moore wins primary for governor
entries.snippet: Rising party star Gov. Wes Moore won the Democratic primary in his bid for reelection to a second term. Republican voters hope to return the state to GOP leadership by picking a candidate they think can unseat him.

entries.title: Wilson wins GOP nomination for South Carolina governor after Trump hedges his bet on race
entries.snippet: South Carolina Attorney General Alan Wilson won a runoff election on Tuesday, swiftly routing the candidate initially endorsed by President Donald Trump to be the Republican nominee for governor.

entries.title: Trains across Germany halted for hours by communication system outage
entries.snippet: The main national railway operator, Deutsche Bahn, said shortly before 1 a.m. — nearly 2 1/2 hours after it first reported the outage — that the problem had been resolved and service was resuming "step by step."

entries.snippet: The ruling was a big victory for the Republican administration, which views the expansion of so-called expedited removal as a key tool for carrying out its mass deportation policy.

entries.title: Read the House transcripts of Bill Gates and Lesley Groff's interviews in Epstein probe
entries.snippet: The House Oversight Committee on Tuesday released transcripts of the testimonies by Bill Gates and Lesley Groff in closed-door depositions before the panel in June as part of its investigation into the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

entries.title: The reflecting pool is about to be drained, again. Here's what to know
entries.snippet: Green water, floating liner chunks, and workers dumping jugs of hydrogen peroxide. These are the images that have characterized the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in the weeks since its reopening following President Donald Trump's ordered renovations.

entries.title: Southeast Asia boost defense ties but avoids firm alliances
entries.snippet: Countries across the region are expanding defense cooperation in ways that change the South China Sea equation but fall short of a new anti-China bloc.

entries.title: Trump offers Iran an economic lifeline — with strings
entries.snippet: Iran has seen a speedy rebound in oil exports after the US-Iran deal granted immediate waivers on US sanctions. Relief on frozen assets and a $300 billion reconstruction fund now hinge on Tehran meeting key conditions.

entries.title: North Korean soldier crosses border to South
entries.snippet: South Korea's military says it is investigating the soldier's reasons for crossing the inner-Korean border. While dozens of North Koreans flee each year, usually via China, crossing directly south is very rare.

entries.title: India news: Protests in northern region Ladakh over talks with Delhi
entries.snippet: Businesses in both northern Leh and Kargil districts remained shut to protest the alleged retraction of key constitutional and administrative agreements. Follow DW for more.

entries.title: China detains two Japanese nationals on smuggling charges
entries.snippet: China has detained two Japanese nationals on suspicion of smuggling banned goods. Reports suggest that at least one case may involve strategic rare-earth-related exports.

entries.title: World Cup: Why Mexico may be LA's favorite team
entries.snippet: Mexican-American football fans in the USA often split allegiances between their two cultures. For many in Los Angeles, the Mexico national team trumps the nation they call home.

entries.title: Heat wave: Alcohol can be a serious danger to your health
entries.snippet: Summer, the FIFA World Cup and a cold beer. Sounds like a dream? Be careful, though; the combination of heat and alcohol can quickly take a very bad turn.

entries.title: Iranian nuclear inspections 'going to happen,' IAEA head
entries.snippet: After contradicting US and Iranian statements, the UN nuclear agency said inspections of Iran's nuclear sites would take place. Iran's top negotiator called the US-Iran deal "America's declaration of defeat." More at DW.

entries.title: Why Austrian author Ingeborg Bachmann remains a literary icon
entries.snippet: A new documentary featuring Sandra Hüller celebrates the Austrian poet and author who was a literary star of her era. She would have turned 100 this year.

entries.title: How Africa's youth wants to save democracy
entries.snippet: Africa's young population often finds itself facing aging, autocratic rulers. Unwilling to settle for democratic rituals alone, many are searching for creative new ways to shape their future.

entries.title: US: Senate vote calls for an end to Trump's Iran war in rare bipartisan rebuke
entries.snippet: Trump criticized the largely symbolic Senate resolution as "meaningless" after several Republicans joined Democrats in a rare break with the White House.

entries.title: Germany news: Major warship project to be scrapped
entries.snippet: The Defense Ministry is dropping a multi-billion-euro project to build F126 frigates, media say. And train services have resumed after a communications glitch overnight halted Germany's rail network . DW has more.

entries.title: US: Google's YouTube settles teen mental health lawsuit
entries.snippet: A Florida teenager said YouTube's addictive design contributed to depression, anxiety and sleep loss. Instagram, Snapchat and TikTok are also facing similar allegations about their impact on young users.

entries.title: Trains resume after radio issue resolved, Deutsche Bahn says
entries.snippet: Train services across Germany have resumed following a technical meltdown on Tuesday night. But regional and suburban rail operators warned that continued delays were possible into Wednesday morning.

entries.title: Ebola in DR Congo sees record first-month caseload
entries.snippet: The UN says the DR Congo has reported 1,000 Ebola cases, the most ever in the first month of any Ebola outbreak in Africa. Meanwhile, Kenya's health minister says he is halting a US-backed Ebola quarantine center.

entries.title: Lebanon's lose-lose: Is there another way out of conflict?
entries.snippet: The new US-Iran peace deal seems to be forcing Lebanon to choose between Israel's sphere of influence or Iran's. It wants neither. But could there be a better alternative, achieved with the help of regional diplomacy?

entries.title: Curacao's trailblazing doctor at the World Cup
entries.snippet: Suzanne Huurman is the only female chief doctor at the 2026 World Cup. Her work is inspiring change in men's football.

entries.title: Poland, Ukraine: Dispute between two close allies deepens
entries.snippet: Polish President Karol Nawrocki last week stripped Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of Poland's highest state honor. How did it come to this? And what has it got to do with next year's election in Poland?

entries.title: Scotland: Sturgeon's ex-husband Peter Murrell jailed for 5 years and 3 months
entries.snippet: Peter Murrell pleaded guilty to embezzling funds in his role as chief executive of the Scottish National Party. He held the SNP's purse strings while his then-wife, Nicola Sturgeon, was Scottish First Minister.
